title: The United Kingdom
intro: Capital cities, mountains, rivers and seas of the UK.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Scotland?
questions.explanation: Edinburgh is the capital of Scotland and is famous for its castle.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Wales?
questions.explanation: Cardiff, in south Wales, is the capital city of Wales.

questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Northern Ireland?
questions.explanation: Belfast is the capital of Northern Ireland. Dublin is the capital of the Republic of Ireland.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in the UK?
questions.explanation: Ben Nevis, in the Scottish Highlands, is the UK's highest mountain at about 1,345 metres.

questions.prompt: Which river flows through London?
questions.explanation: The River Thames flows through the middle of London on its way to the North Sea.

questions.prompt: The English Channel separates England from France.
questions.explanation: The English Channel is the stretch of sea between southern England and northern France.

questions.prompt: Which sea lies to the east of England?
questions.explanation: The North Sea lies between the east coast of Great Britain and countries such as Norway, Denmark and the Netherlands.

questions.prompt: Which of the four countries of the UK has the most people?
questions.explanation: England has by far the largest population of the four countries in the UK.

questions.prompt: On a compass, which direction is opposite north?
questions.explanation: North and south are opposite each other on a compass, as are east and west.

questions.prompt: What is the longest river in the United Kingdom?
questions.explanation: The Severn starts in the Welsh mountains and flows through Wales and England into the Bristol Channel.

questions.prompt: Which river forms part of the border between England and Scotland?
questions.explanation: For about 27 kilometres of its journey to the North Sea, the River Tweed forms the border between Scotland and England.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in England?
questions.explanation: Scafell Pike, in the Lake District in Cumbria, is 978 metres high.

questions.prompt: Which is the largest lake in the United Kingdom by area?
questions.explanation: Lough Neagh, in Northern Ireland, covers more area than any other lake in the UK.

questions.prompt: Which range of hills is often called 'the backbone of England'?
questions.explanation: The Pennines run from north to south through northern England, a bit like a spine down a back.

questions.prompt: Which famous coastline of about 40,000 rock columns is found in Northern Ireland?
questions.explanation: The Giant's Causeway was formed when lava from ancient volcanoes cooled and cracked into many-sided columns.

questions.prompt: Which sea lies between Great Britain and Ireland?
questions.explanation: The Irish Sea separates the island of Great Britain from the island of Ireland. Ferries cross it every day.

questions.prompt: Which of these is a county in England?
questions.explanation: Kent is a county in south-east England, often called 'the Garden of England' because of its orchards and farms.

questions.prompt: On a map, what do contour lines show?

options.label: The height and shape of the land

questions.explanation: Contour lines join places of the same height. When they are close together, the land is steep.

questions.prompt: Which compass direction is halfway between north and east?
questions.explanation: On an eight-point compass, north-east sits exactly halfway between north and east.

questions.prompt: When you read a grid reference on a map, which numbers do you read first?

options.label: The numbers along the bottom of the map
The numbers up the side of the map

questions.explanation: Remember "along the corridor, then up the stairs": read across first (eastings), then up (northings).

questions.prompt: Which city stands on the River Mersey in north-west England?
questions.explanation: Liverpool grew up on the Mersey estuary and became one of Britain's biggest ports.

questions.prompt: What is the national flag of the United Kingdom called?

options.label: The Union Flag, or Union Jack

questions.explanation: The Union Flag combines the crosses of St George (England), St Andrew (Scotland) and St Patrick (Ireland).

questions.prompt: Which country of the United Kingdom has a red dragon on its flag?
questions.explanation: The Welsh flag shows a red dragon on a background of green and white.

questions.prompt: Which country of the United Kingdom is not on the island of Great Britain?
questions.explanation: Great Britain is the island with England, Scotland and Wales. Northern Ireland is on the island of Ireland.

questions.prompt: The Isle of Man is part of the United Kingdom.
questions.explanation: The Isle of Man has its own parliament, called Tynwald. It is a Crown Dependency, not part of the UK.

questions.prompt: The Lake District is a national park in north-west England.
questions.explanation: The Lake District, in Cumbria, is famous for its lakes, valleys and fells, including Scafell Pike.

questions.prompt: Scotland has more islands than any other country of the United Kingdom.
questions.explanation: Scotland has hundreds of islands, including the Hebrides, Orkney and Shetland.

questions.prompt: London is the capital city of the whole United Kingdom, as well as of England.
questions.explanation: London is the capital of England and of the UK. The UK Parliament meets there, in the Palace of Westminster.

questions.prompt: Ben Nevis is the highest mountain in the UK. About how high is it, in metres?
questions.explanation: Ben Nevis is about 1,345 metres high. It stands near the town of Fort William in the Scottish Highlands.

questions.prompt: About how long is the River Thames, in kilometres?
questions.explanation: The Thames is about 346 kilometres long. It flows from the Cotswolds, through London, to the North Sea.
